financing.summary: Risewell Homes (legal issuer now Risewell Homes, Inc., formerly The New Home Company Inc.) is a private, Apollo-fund-owned builder that calls itself asset-light and funds itself with three tools: Apollo equity ($650M of new equity for the Landsea deal), Rule 144A senior unsecured notes (about $775M face across a 9.25% 2029 issue and an 8.5% 2030 issue) plus a $600M revolver, and land banking. Its one public land-bank relationship is with Kennedy Lewis / Millrose: a $700M commitment signed 2025-05-12, of which Millrose funded $494.5M net at the Landsea closing for 4,186 homesites optioned back to the builder. It controlled about 28,000 lots at the December 2025 rebrand, but no owned-versus-optioned split has been published since the Landsea take-private, because quarterly reports go only to registered bondholders. For a land banker the opening is that the Kennedy Lewis program covers only about 15% of the controlled lots, the unfunded part of the $700M (up to $100M of it for horizontal development) is not reported as drawn, and S&P rated the credit 'B' (CreditWatch positive) in 2025, so land-light capital is how this sponsor-owned builder grows.
financing.land_strategy: Asset-light in its own words: New Home described itself as a "diversified asset-light homebuilder" in the Landsea tender documents and on Risewell's investor page, and CEO Matthew Zaist told The Builder's Daily the thesis is to scale operations without owning more land than necessary. No published target for the share of lots optioned. Before the deal, Landsea (the larger half) controlled 55% of its 10,516 lots by option or purchase contract at 2025-03-31 and aimed for 3 to 4 years of supply on a 24 to 36 month development horizon.

lots.source_title: New Home Co. and Landsea Homes Unite Under New National Brand: Risewell Homes (company release via PRWeb, 2025-12-02)
lots.note: About 28,000 lots controlled (company's rounded figure), with 120+ actively selling communities in 11 markets across 7 states. No owned or optioned split is public since the take-private. Latest public split is Landsea alone at 2025-03-31: 4,710 owned, 5,806 controlled by option or purchase contract, 10,516 total (55.2% controlled, calculated); see https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1721386/000172138625000018/lhi-20250331.htm. At least 4,186 homesites are optioned from Millrose (Kennedy Lewis program) since 2025-06-25.

land_banking.description: Land bank commitment letter ('Project Lakeland') signed 2025-05-12: up to $700M, 100% provided by KLIM, with up to $600M funded at the Landsea closing and up to $100M for horizontal development afterwards. KLIM buys properties and grants homesite options (and construction agreements up to a guaranteed contract sum). Option terms run up to 72 months, and properties are grouped in pools of at least four projects with cross-termination and a $20M cap per pool on the builder's total payment obligation. Total takedown price must be at least 105.25% of the closing commitment. It was conditioned on at least $650M of sponsor equity. Fees (initial option fee, monthly option fee, termination fee, asset management fee, minimum project return) are in an unfiled fee letter.
land_banking.source_title: Land Bank Commitment Letter, KLIM to The New Home Company Inc., 2025-05-12 (Landsea Schedule TO Ex. (b)(1))
land_banking.note: Signed by Darren Richman for KLIM and Miek Harbur (EVP, General Counsel and Secretary) for New Home. Funding was placed with Millrose (next row). Neither the builder nor Millrose has published whether the remaining ~$205M of the commitment (including the $100M horizontal tranche) was drawn.

land_banking.description: At the Landsea closing on 2025-06-25 Millrose bought $522.8M of land (4,186 homesites), paying $494.5M in cash net of $28.3M of builder option deposits, and optioned the homesites back to New Home. Millrose's FY2025 10-K counts this as part of the up-to-$700M commitment, and its Q3 2026 deck lists New Home / Landsea as one of three builder M&A deals it has financed ($700M of land assets, 4,186 homesites).
land_banking.source_title: Millrose Properties FY2025 10-K, Note 3 Spin-Off and Other Significant Business Transactions
land_banking.note: Deposit equals about 5.4% of land value (calculated), well below the roughly 10.5% on Millrose's Lennar book. The homesites span five states (Cox Castle, Millrose counsel, 2025-07-21), and Millrose financed the purchase from a $1.0B Goldman-led delayed-draw term loan, since refinanced. Corroborated by https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2017206/000119312526432747/ck0002017206-ex99_2.htm (Millrose Q3 2026 deck).

ma.description: Apollo-owned New Home Co., through Lido Holdco / Lido Merger Sub, bought Landsea for $11.30 a share in cash (about $1.2B enterprise value, 61% premium). The deal was announced 2025-05-12 and closed 2025-06-25 after 83.27% of shares were tendered. It was funded with $650M of Apollo equity, Kennedy Lewis/Millrose land-bank capital and New Home senior notes. Landsea was delisted, its board resigned and all its executive officers left. The combined company rebranded as Risewell Homes on 2025-12-02.
ma.map_impact: Landsea (2024 Builder #33) is absorbed and the combined company is the #27 row (Risewell Homes; New Home was #62). Footprint is now 11 markets in 7 states (AZ, CA, CO, FL, OR, TX, WA), about 28,000 controlled lots and about 4,000 closings a year. New Home's team runs it: Matthew Zaist CEO, Robert Irwin CFO, John Bohnen COO, Miek Harbur GC, Matthew Gibson EVP Investments. Landsea's land and finance contacts are gone (e.g. its president/COO Michael Forsum now leads Strata Land Partners). Millrose holds 4,186 of the homesites under option.
ma.source_title: Landsea Homes Corp. 8-K filed 2025-06-25 (completion of merger)
ma.note: Deal value and financing mix from the joint release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1721386/000173112225000715/e6593_ex99-1.htm). Rebrand and footprint from the PRWeb release of 2025-12-02.
